title: Satwik and Chirag Have Won the Singapore Open. It Is Their First Title in Two Years.
excerpt: The Indian doubles pair beat Indonesia's Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Shohibul Fikri in a three-game final after ending the world No. 1 pair's 34-match unbeaten run in the semifinals.
body:
Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty are Singapore Open champions. The Indian pair beat Indonesia's Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Shohibul Fikri 18-21, 21-17, 21-16 in the final on Sunday to claim their first BWF World Tour title in two years.

It is the biggest title of their 2026 season. After finishing as runners-up at the Thailand Open last week, where they lost to another Indonesian pair in straight games, Satwik and Chirag left Singapore with the trophy and the validation that their best badminton is still ahead of them.

## The Road to the Title

The story of their Singapore Open campaign will be remembered less for the final itself and more for what happened twenty-four hours before it. In Saturday's semifinal, Satwik and Chirag did something no pair had managed in seven months — they beat Kim Won Ho and Seo Seung Jae.

The South Korean duo, reigning world champions and the world's No. 1 ranked pair, had been on a 34-match unbeaten streak dating back to the 2025 Denmark Open. They had beaten the Indians twice before, at the Malaysia Open and China Masters. But in Singapore, the fourth-seeded Indian pair fought back from 8-13 down in the first game, clawed back from 11-14 in the second, and won 21-19, 21-18 in 52 relentless minutes.

"When we were down, we kept calm and backed ourselves because we knew if we stuck to our plan, they would crack at some point," Chirag said after the semifinal.

## A Final Won on Nerve

The final against Fajar and Fikri, seeded third, was a different kind of contest. The Indonesian pair took the first game 21-18, and for a moment the Thailand Open heartbreak seemed to be repeating itself. But Satwik and Chirag responded with a composed second game, winning 21-17, and then pulled away decisively in the decider with a 21-16 scoreline that flattered the Indonesians.

The victory makes them only the second Indian pair to win the Singapore Open title. B Sai Pratheek won it in 2017. Saina Nehwal and PV Sindhu both reached the final — in 2010 and 2022 respectively — but neither won.

## Breaking the Title Drought

The title drought had been a growing concern. Satwik and Chirag's last BWF World Tour title came two years ago, and the pressure of being India's most consistent doubles pair without a trophy to show for it in 2025 and early 2026 had begun to mount. Their loss in the Thailand Open final last week only amplified the narrative.

But this week they answered every question. They beat the world champions, they came from behind in the final, and they won it in the decider when the pressure was at its highest.

## What It Means for the NRI Fan

For Indian badminton fans in the diaspora — many of whom watched Satwik and Chirag's rise from Thomas Cup heroes to Commonwealth Games champions — this Singapore Open title is a reminder that India's men's doubles programme is no longer a curiosity. It is a genuine force.

With the Asian Games approaching in September and the Olympics cycle beginning to take shape, Satwik and Chirag are now the pair every top doubles combination in the world will be studying. The 34-match streak they ended in the semifinal? That was not just a streak. That was a statement of intent — for Singapore, and for everything that comes next.

The Indian pair's next assignment will be the Indonesia Open, where they will look to build on this momentum and establish themselves as the pair to beat in the second half of 2026.
